title: Accelerated community multi cancer diagnostic evaluation platform
official: AcceleRated community Multi cAncer DIagnostic evaLuatiOn platform (ARMADILO)
summary:
Background and study aims
Many people visit their GP with symptoms such as abdominal pain, loss of appetite, bloating, nausea or unexplained weight loss. These symptoms are common and are often caused by conditions other than cancer, but they can sometimes be a sign of cancer. Because these symptoms can have many different causes, it can be difficult for GPs to decide which patients should be referred to hospital for specialist cancer tests.
Multi-cancer blood tests are new types of blood tests that look for signals associated with several different types of cancer. They could potentially help GPs decide which patients need further investigation. Before these tests can be used routinely in the NHS, researchers need to understand how accurately they identify people who do and do not have cancer.
The ARMADILO study aims to assess several multi-cancer blood tests in people aged 50 years or over who are having NHS blood tests because they have symptoms that could have a number of causes, including cancer. The researchers will compare the multi-cancer test results with information from participants' NHS health records to assess how accurately the tests identify people who are diagnosed with cancer.
This is an observational study, so taking part will not change a participant's medical care. The multi-cancer test results will not be given to participants nor their GPs and will not be used to make decisions about care because the accuracy of the tests is not yet known. Participants will continue to receive their usual NHS investigations and care.

Who can participate?
People may be able to take part if they:
1. Are aged 50 years or over
2. Are having a blood test in NHS primary care to investigate at least one of the following symptoms: abdominal pain, loss of appetite, bloating, nausea or weight loss
3. Are willing and able to give informed consent; and
4. Are willing and able to provide a blood sample for the research.
People cannot take part if they have already joined the ARMADILO study, or if they have had certain invasive cancers or cancers of the blood, bone marrow or lymphatic system, or definitive treatment for these cancers, within the previous three years. Some treatments, such as adjuvant hormone therapy, are allowed.

What does the study involve?
People who decide to take part will have one study visit. Where possible, this will take place at the same time as their usual NHS appointment for a blood test. In some areas, the study blood sample may instead be taken at the participant's home or another suitable community location.
Participants will be asked to give one blood sample of up to 80 ml, answer some questions about themselves and their health, and give permission for researchers to obtain information from their medical records, including GP, hospital and central NHS records.
There are no further routine study visits. Participants' health records will be followed for at least 12 months to find out whether they are diagnosed with cancer. Participants will also be asked for permission for their records to potentially be followed for up to 5 years to investigate longer-term cancer and non-cancer outcomes.
The donated blood will be used to assess different multi-cancer tests. Participants and their GPs will not receive the results of these tests. 
Some participants may also be invited to take part in an interview about their experience of the study. This will help the researchers understand how acceptable and practical the study procedures are and whether there are barriers that make it more difficult for some groups of people to take part.
 
What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
There is no expected direct medical benefit to people who take part. In particular, taking part will not provide an earlier diagnosis or additional information about the cause of a participant's symptoms because the multi-cancer test results will not be returned. Participants' normal NHS investigations and care will continue regardless of whether they take part.
The information collected may help researchers determine whether multi-cancer blood tests could be useful in the NHS in the future. If suitable tests are identified and subsequently shown to work in further studies, they could potentially help GPs decide which patients need specialist cancer investigations and contribute to earlier diagnosis for future patients.
The main physical risks are those associated with having blood taken. These include temporary discomfort, bruising or light-headedness and a small risk of infection. Where possible, the research blood will be collected at the same time and using the same needle as the participant's routine NHS blood test, although in some circumstances an additional blood-taking appointment may be needed.

Where is the study run from?
The study is being led by researchers at the University of Oxford, Nuffield Department of Primary Care Health Sciences (UK). Recruitment will take place across approximately 132 primary care sites.  The study is sponsored by the University of Oxford and is coordinated through the Oxford Collaborative Clinical Trials Unit.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
October 2026 to September 2030

Who is funding the study?
The study is funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR), Efficacy and Mechanism Evaluation programme (UK).

Who is the main contact?
ARMADILO Study Team, armadilo_pcctu@phc.ox.ac.uk

interventions.name:
This is a single-arm prospective observational multicentre cohort study.

Potential participants will be identified either opportunistically when they see their GP or through regular searches of recent presentations at the GP practice. Eligible patients will be forwarded the Participant Information

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Willing and able to give informed consent for participation in the study
2. Aged 50 years or above
3. Having a blood test in NHS primary care for the investigation of at least one of the following non-specific symptoms: abdominal pain, appetite loss, bloating, nausea, weight loss
4. Willing and able to donate a blood sample for research

Study participants for the qualitative component: 
1. Practice staff involved in delivering the study at sites including practice managers, GPs, nurses, receptionists and other practice staff
2. Patient participants: same criteria as for main study, but interviews may also include carers and/or family members involved in their care
Exclusion criteria:
1. Previously enrolled in this study
2. A history of invasive or haematological malignancy (cancers affecting blood, bone marrow and lymphatic system) diagnosed within the past 3 years
3. Has undergone definitive treatment for invasive or haematological malignancy in the past 3 years (adjuvant hormone therapy is permissible in this context)
